config.title: Build web worker integration for expensive calculations

intro.title: Build web worker integration for expensive calculations
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web page that uses a Web Worker to perform a heavy calculation in the background, preventing the main interface from freezing. You will learn how to offload expensive computations to a separate thread to keep your web application responsive. The core concepts involve creating a Web Worker, sending messages to it, and handling the results it returns. You'll work with JavaScript's Worker API, message passing via postMessage, and event listeners for handling responses.
intro.usecase: Web workers are essential for maintaining responsive interfaces when performing heavy computations in real applications. In data dashboards, they enable smooth chart rendering while calculating complex statistics from large datasets. Image editing tools use web workers to apply filters and transformations without freezing the UI. Financial applications leverage them for real-time risk calculations and algorithmic trading simulations. Even in e-commerce sites, web workers can handle complex price calculations and inventory checks during checkout processes.

objectives: Initialize a web worker with a separate JavaScript file for background execution
Configure message event listeners to handle communication between the main thread and worker
Implement a calculation function within the web worker that processes data received via messages
Construct a postMessage call from the main thread to send data to the web worker
Manipulate the DOM to display calculation results returned from the web worker
Integrate error handling for web worker loading failures and runtime errors
Control the web worker lifecycle by properly terminating it when calculations are complete

steps.title: Import required APIs for web worker and UI
steps.instruction: Import useState from 'react' for state management and create a reference for the web worker using useRef.
steps.hint: You'll need to import both useState and useRef from 'react' to manage state and create a worker reference.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing hooks for state and refs
import { useState, useRef } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for useState and useRef are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: useState and useRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both useState and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing both useState and useRef from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Initialize state for calculation results
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to declare a state variable named 'result' with an initial value of null.

steps.analogousExample:

const [data, setData] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable ready to store the calculation result from the web worker.
successCriteria: The App component contains a useState call that declares a 'result' state variable initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The state variable wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState with null to create a 'result' state variable.

steps.title: Initialize state for loading status
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a state variable called 'isLoading' using useState, defaulting to false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should be named 'isLoading' and initially set to false.

const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your App component will have a state variable 'isLoading' that tracks whether the web worker is currently processing a calculation.
successCriteria: The 'isLoading' state variable is declared using useState with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the useState hook to declare a variable named 'isLoading' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a state variable called 'isLoading' that starts as false, using the useState hook.

steps.title: Create a web worker instance reference
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a reference using useRef to store the web worker instance. Name it workerRef and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Use the useRef hook to create a mutable reference that will hold the web worker object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A workerRef variable is created using useRef and initialized to null, ready to store the web worker instance.
successCriteria: The workerRef is declared with useRef and initialized to null inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useRef and initializing it to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to create a reference using useRef and name it workerRef.

steps.title: Define handler to start expensive calculation
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a function named handleStartCalculation that initializes a new Worker and sends a message to start the calculation.
steps.hint: Define a function that creates a new Worker instance using the worker reference, sets up an onmessage handler to receive results, and posts a message to the worker.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now contains a handleStartCalculation function that creates a Worker, sets up message handling, and posts a calculation request.
successCriteria: A function named handleStartCalculation is defined inside the App component, it creates a new Worker, sets an onmessage handler, and posts a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handler function, but make sure it creates a Worker, sets up message handling, and posts a calculation request.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function is missing or incomplete. Create a function named handleStartCalculation that initializes a Worker and sends a calculation message.

steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element that shows 'Calculating...' when isLoading is true. Place it below the button in the return statement.
steps.hint:

Calculating...

: null}

successCriteria: A paragraph element with the text 'Calculating...' is conditionally rendered using isLoading state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the isLoading state variable and the ternary operator syntax correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading status paragraph isn't properly implemented. Check that you're using the isLoading state and conditional rendering syntax.

steps.title: Display calculation result in UI
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the div that displays the calculation result when it's available. Use the result state variable and conditional rendering to only show the paragraph when result is not null.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or logical && operator to conditionally render the paragraph. The paragraph should display something like 'Result: ' followed by the result value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the calculation result when it's available, appearing below the loading message after the calculation completes.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that conditionally displays the result value when result is not null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some UI for the result, but check that it only displays when result has a value (not null). Make sure you're using the result state variable correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The result isn't displaying properly. Remember to add a paragraph element that shows the result value only when result is not null. You can use conditional rendering with a ternary operator or logical &&.
